name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.28.0 (2026-08-27) is a hardening release that caps cache replay at 10 MB per topic, limits message titles to 1 KB and tags to 512 bytes, and applies the visitor bandwidth limit to poll-based cache replays. v2.27.0 (2026-08-04) added email-based login, hardened message templating against memory abuse, and promoted PostgreSQL support out of experimental status. v2.26.x addressed a CPU denial-of-service via message templates, added configurable date/time formats in the web app, and introduced an abuse ban-feed mechanism for self-hosters. Full release notes are available at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL (clients); see repository for details
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, most recently v2.28.0 on 2026-08-27
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password, access tokens, email-based login, and topic-level access control
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud service

breaking_excerpts: Message titles are now limited to 1 KB and all tags combined to 512 bytes; larger requests are rejected with HTTP 400 (error codes 40057/40058).

visitor-attachment-daily-bandwidth-limit now also covers poll-based cache replays; polls beyond the budget are rejected with HTTP 429 (error code 42905). Operators serving both attachments and heavy pollers may need to raise the limit.
Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first, or delete the cache database.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but functions as a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications with file and link sharing but is a proprietary cloud-only service with a limited free tier, unlike ntfy's fully open and self-hostable approach.

alternatives.name: Ntopng / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager is a powerful open-source alerting tool tightly integrated with Prometheus metrics, but it is infrastructure-focused and far more complex to configure compared to ntfy's simple HTTP pub-sub model.
